response: In simple terms, gravity is the invisible force that pulls objects toward each other. It is what keeps your feet on the ground, makes apples fall from trees, and holds the planets in orbit around the Sun. Anything that has mass—whether it is a tiny pebble or a giant star—has gravity, and the more massive an object is, the stronger its gravitational pull. This force works across space, growing weaker as objects move farther apart but never completely disappearing. It governs the structure of galaxies, the rise and fall of ocean tides, and the very air we breathe by keeping it wrapped around our planet. Without gravity, the universe as we know it would simply drift apart into chaos. That is gravity.
